body: # Description Implemented a new Paid Labor Cost component with an interactive grouped bar chart displaying project labor costs with comprehensive filtering capabilities. Implements - Create Paid Labor Cost chart in the "Weekly Project Summary" (http://localhost:3000/bmdashboard/totalconstructionsummary or reports -> total construction summary) ## Related PRS (if any): N/A ## Main changes explained: - Created new PaidLaborCost.jsx component with grouped bar chart visualization using Chart.js - Implemented custom PaidLaborCostDatePicker.jsx component for intuitive date range selection - Added comprehensive namespaced CSS styles in PaidLaborCost.css with the paid-labor-cost- prefix to prevent style conflicts - Built interactive filtering functionality for projects, tasks, and date ranges - Implemented data aggregation logic to display appropriate metrics based on filter selections - Added hover tooltips for detailed cost information display - Ensured proper API communication with POST method for data retrieval ## How to test: 1. Check out the current branch 2. Run npm install and npm start to run this PR locally 3. Clear site data/cache 4. Log in as admin user 5. Go to Reports → Total Construction Summary -> Labor and Time Tracking 2nd card 6. Verify the new Paid Labor Cost component appears with the grouped bar chart 7. Test the filtering functionality: - Select different projects from the Project filter - Select different tasks from the Tasks filter - Use the Date filter to select a custom date range 8. Hover over bars to verify tooltip information shows the project name, task, and cost value 9. Verify "All Projects" selection shows the total project cost and costs for the two most expensive tasks 10. Check the browser console to confirm no errors are present ## Screenshots or videos of changes: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ece293f5-6bc0-44f0-b758-34492bd717c0 ## Note: This PR introduces a completely new Paid Labor Cost dashboard component that meets all specified requirements: - Grouped bar chart with project names on X-axis and costs on Y-axis - Color-coded legend for different cost types - Interactive filters for projects, tasks, and date ranges - Hover functionality to display detailed cost information - Proper handling of "All Projects" view with aggregated data - Custom date picker implementation for intuitive date range selection - Responsive design that adjusts to different screen sizes ## Important: The backend API for this component is not yet implemented. The component currently makes an API call structure but falls back to mock data when the API is unavailable. Once the backend implementation is completed, this component will be fully integrated with the actual data.

body:
Dependent on / followup to https://github.com/grafana/loki/pull/17311

# Implement Projection Pipeline in Engine Executor

## Changes

This PR adds projection support to the Loki query engine executor, allowing queries to select specific columns from record batches. Key changes include:

- Add `NewProjectPipeline` function for creating projection pipelines
- Implement the previously unimplemented `executeProjection` method
- Add `evaluator` field to the `Context` struct for expression evaluation
- Improve CSV to Arrow conversion by trimming whitespace
- Add comprehensive test cases for projections

## Test Coverage

The implementation includes thorough tests that verify:
- Single column projection
- Multiple column projection
- Column reordering
- Processing multiple input batches

body:
MFDNN-13451

Thanks to @echeresh, who pivoted all the optimizations from the tracker and provided a PoC for them.

This PR implements 4 out of 6 of specified in the tracker. 2 not included is check_zero_pad on inputs and simplified RNG-related filling changes.

On a list attached to the tracker the speed up looks like this:
Before:
```
total: 76.37s; create_pd: 0.04s (0%); create_prim: 7.55s (10%); fill: 31.24s (41%); execute: 2.17s (3%); compute_ref: 9.06s (12%); compare: 23.82s (31%);
```
After:
```
total: 54.19s; create_pd: 0.04s (0%); create_prim: 7.19s (13%); fill: 19.07s (35%); execute: 2.13s (4%); compute_ref: 8.65s (16%); compare: 15.23s (28%);
```

## Changes Made
1. Added proper requirements.txt with all necessary dependencies

   - Using webdriver-manager for automatic driver management
   - Added Mac-specific Chrome options for better stability

   - Better absolute path handling throughout the codebase

These changes have been tested and confirmed working on macOS with:
- Chrome browser
- ffmpeg installed via Homebrew
- Python 3.x

Added clear instructions for macOS setup in the documentation:

3. Copy config.example.json to config.json and add your credentials

The changes maintain compatibility with other platforms while adding proper macOS support.

author: cfrantz
body:
We cannot record clean/modified status because this affects build reproducibility during ROM_EXT signing.

During a signing ceremony:
- First we generate pre-signing artifacts, typically in a clean codebase.
- Next, we take hashes of the pre-signing artifacts offline and sign them with our signing infrastructure.
- Finally, we bring the offline signatures back to the codebase and land them in an appropriate `signatures` subdirectory.  This modifies the codebase, which then causes a change in the build_status value, which causes bazel to rebuild pre-signing artifacts, which invalidates the signatures.

body:
## Purpose

Currently, this is the behavior of `dwnl.exe`, on large files,

```
C:\dwnl>dwnl https://github.com/win32ss/supermium/releases/download/v132-r2/supe
rmium_132_32_setup.exe DL1.exe
--2025-04-17 16:33:24-- https://github.com/win32ss/supermium/releases/download/v
132-r2/supermium_132_32_setup.exe
        => DL1.exe
Connecting to 4.237.22.38... done.
Sending request... Connecting to 185.199.108.133... done.
Sending request... done.
Length: 106478533 [application/x-msdownload]

99% (106471168 byte(s) downloaded)
File saved.
```

Notice that the progression stops at **99%** AND **Length: 106478533** does **NOT** match **106471168 byte(s) downloaded**

This Push Request aims to fix this experience

## Proposed changes

The following changes were made

* CBindStatusCallback_UpdateProgress - Rework the failsafe check to enable percentage to be at 100%
* CBindStatusCallback_UpdateProgress - More thorough failsafe check, to avoid displaying 100% (or even 101%) where the actual and expected file sizes don't match
* `case BINDSTATUS_ENDDOWNLOADDATA` - Do update the progress one last time to be at 100%, on download success

### New behavior

The result is now:

```
C:\dwnl>dwnl-100 https://github.com/win32ss/supermium/releases/download/v132-r2/
supermium_132_32_setup.exe DL2.exe

Connecting to 4.237.22.38... done.
Sending request... Connecting to 185.199.108.133... done.
Sending request... done.
Length: 106478533 [application/x-msdownload]

100% (106478533 byte(s) downloaded)
File saved.
```

body:
## Overview

Updates the `go-ethereum` dependency in `proxyd` to the latest version (`v1.15.8`). [`v1.15.1`](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/releases/tag/v1.15.1) included support for EIP-7702 transactions in the transaction pool, and we're currently still one release behind.

This is currently causing an issue on Sepolia chains that have activated Isthmus, where EIP-7702 transactions aren't being accepted.

author: soyersoyer
body:
The zero data detection causes an audible spike after 21ms of silence.

Add an UnZeroData option to the minidexed.ini file that sets the last sample of the chunk to 1 if it is zero.

The spec says:
Zero Data Detect
 The PCM510x has a zero-data detect function. When the device detects continuous zero data, it enters a full analog mute condition.
The PCM510x counts zero data over 1024LRCKs (21ms @ 48kHz) before setting analog mute.

author: aromarious
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes the issue where user messages are incorrectly sent to stdout instead of stderr, which causes JSON parsing failures in the MCP communication protocol.

## Problem
The MCP server uses stdout for JSON-based communication. However, when user messages (like initialization logs) are sent to stdout instead of stderr, they interfere with this protocol, causing parsing errors like:

```
Failed to parse message: "[GlobalSettings] Allowed base directory set to: /path/to/directory\n"
```

## Changes
This PR modifies the global-settings.ts file to redirect user messages from console.log() to console.error(), ensuring they go to stderr instead of stdout:

```typescript
// Before
console.log(`[GlobalSettings] Allowed base directory set to: ${this._allowedBaseDir}`);

// After
console.error(`[GlobalSettings] Allowed base directory set to: ${this._allowedBaseDir}`);
```

## Testing
Tested by verifying messages now appear in stderr and no longer cause JSON parsing errors in the client.

author: aromarious
body:
## Summary
This PR improves error reporting in the MCP server to provide more detailed error messages in the inspector console.

## Problem
Currently, many errors in the codebase are converted to string using `String(error)`, which often results in unhelpful `[object Object]` messages in the inspector console. This makes debugging difficult as error details are lost.

## Changes
This PR changes how errors are displayed in console output and returned from API calls:

```typescript
// Before
`Error: ${String(error)}`

// After
`Error: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : JSON.stringify(error, null, 2)}`
```

This improvement provides more detailed error information by:
1. Using error.message for standard Error objects
2. Using JSON.stringify for other error objects, ensuring all properties are displayed
3. Adding proper indentation for better readability

## Affected Files
This change has been applied to error handling in:
1. `/src/resources/diff.ts`
2. `/src/resources/file.ts`
3. `/src/resources/history.ts`
4. `/src/resources/repository.ts`
5. `/src/tools/advanced.ts`
6. `/src/tools/branch.ts`
7. `/src/tools/remote.ts`
8. `/src/tools/repository.ts`
9. `/src/tools/workdir.ts`

## Testing
Manually tested by triggering various error conditions and verifying that error messages now show detailed information instead of "[object Object]".

body:
This runs the https://github.com/Vici37/cr-source-typer project on the crystal source code with command:

```
CRYSTAL_PATH="./src" ./typer spec/std_spec.cr --error-trace --exclude src/crystal/ --stats --progress src 
```

Followed by repeated:
```
make spec # error
git checkout <next offending file>
```
Until specs passed and a basic `make` call all work. 

I have done no additional fixing beyond the above - the way that the standard lib is loosely coupled with itself means that the order of `requires` isn't well structured, and so some types were present in restrictions before the relevant `require` was hit. Some methods have hilariously long type restrictions as well.

This PR should not be as accepted as it is, but represents an interesting view of the internals of the compiler and standard library that I wanted to share.

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/DavideDaniel/oss-projects/security/code-scanning/14](https://github.com/DavideDaniel/oss-projects/security/code-scanning/14)

To fix the issue, we will replace the use of `execa.shell` with `execa` (or `execa.command`), which allows us to pass the command and its arguments separately. This avoids the need for shell interpretation and ensures that special characters in the arguments are handled safely. Specifically:
1. Replace the dynamically constructed shell command `` `${__dirname}/copy.sh ${src} ${dest}` `` with a command string for the script (`path.join(__dirname, 'copy.sh')`) and an array of arguments (`[src, dest]`).
2. Update the `execa.shell` call to use `execa` with the command and arguments passed separately.

author: linkdd
body:
## Context

The `state` and `status` fields of the `Container` model in Netbox are only updated when actions are triggered from Netbox.

However, there are cases when the state of the container changes without being triggered by Netbox, such as:

 - the container has a healthcheck, its state begins with `starting` and can transition to `healthy` or `unhealthy`
 - a `running` container can crash and will transition to the `exited` state, or `restarting` if it has a restart policy

The Docker Engine API provides an endpoint to listen for events on many different objects, see [API reference](https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.49/#tag/System/operation/SystemEvents)

In events from containers, we are notified by many types of actions. We are interested by:

 - `start`
 - `restart`
 - `stop`
 - `kill`
 - `oom`
 - `die`
 - `pause`
 - `unpause`

There is the event `update` as well, but it seems to be triggered every second on my machine, and I did not want to DDoS the poor Netbox handling hundreds of containers across many hosts.

Whenever such an event is received, we update the `status` and `state` field of the `Container` model in Netbox.

## Changes

 - [x] :sparkles: Update container's state in Netbox based on Docker Engine events
 - [x] :bookmark: v1.12.0

body:
### What is this???

`main-copy` is a copy of the current `main` branch, the only difference being that its commit history was rebuilt to erase my personal email. All the commit hashes are different, but all code is identical to what's on `main` right now. This is just a simple request to incorporate `main-copy` into `main`.

_**IMPORTANT**_: This PR **should not** be merged directly into `main`, as it may result in many duplicated commits. This PR merely serves to explain what this branch is and what to do with it.

**The right way** to incorporate this `main-copy` branch into `main` is to make a fresh clone of the repo, and run the following commands:

```bash
git checkout main

# Replace the commit history of main with that of main-copy
# This DOES NOT delete any 'real' history (dates/times, commit messages, etc.) — it only replaces some metadata (my personal email)
git reset --hard origin/main-copy

# The '--force' flag is required to overwrite the protected remote branch
git push -u origin main --force
```

It goes without saying, but in order to run that last command, you must have force push rights to the main branch (I do not, which is why I can't do this), or the main branch protection needs to be turned off temporarily.

Note: Contributors will need to re-clone the repo in order to push any further commits

Thanks in advance!

### P.S.

If you are skeptical that the code is exactly the same, just run a diff in the repo:
```bash
git checkout main
git diff origin/main-copy
```

No output == they are the same :)

The only visible difference is that
```bash
git log | grep caden
```
will give you my personal email while checked out to `main` and the same command will only give you my GitHub noreply email while checked out to `main-copy`

author: joe-beaulieu-dev
body:
### Description
- Fix an issue where UI elements on the `CoreScreen` that are visibility-gated by navigation logic would quickly flash on and off the screen under certain conditions.
  - The fix was to move the `currentCoreDestination` and `previousCoreDestination` `State` to `CoreScreenViewModel`, and prevent them from being updated when either `coreNavHostController.currentBackStackEntry.destination` or `secondaryNavHostController.currentBackStackEntry.destination` were `null`. This was done by putting them inside `null` check-gated `LaunchedEffects`. These `LaunchedEffects` also take their respective `NavDestinations` as a key in order to prevent redundant method calls to update the `State`.
  - Bug Example: If you're on the `SettingsScreen` (`CoreScreen`), then navigate away from `CoreScreen` -> `AlarmDefaultsScreen`, when you press back to go back to the `SettingsScreen`, the `LavaFloatingActionButton` and `NextAlarmCloud`, which are supposed to not be shown on the `SettingsScreen`, would very quickly flash on the screen before disappearing to their intended "invisible" state. Furthermore, the `VolcanoNavigationBar` would incorrectly flash "Alarm" as the current screen, before switching to "Settings."
  - This was happening due to the fact that the `NavHostController.currentBackStackEntry` returns `null` when a screen is recreated, such as when navigating from `CoreScreen` -> `AlarmDefaultsScreen` -> `CoreScreen`. Upon going back to `CoreScreen`, its `NavHostController` returns `null` from `NavHostController.currentBackStackEntry` as if it didn't have a back stack. Immediately afterwards it automatically returns the actual `non-null` `NavBackStackEntry` that it should have emitted in the first place, which I was observing as `State`. This `NavBackStackEntry` is converted to a `Destination` via `CoreScreenNavComponent.fromNavBackStackEntry()`, which defaults to `Destination.AlarmListScreen` if the `NavBackStackEntry` is `null`. Without getting into the visibility-gating logic of the aforementioned `CoreScreen` UI elements, this default of `Destination.AlarmListScreen`, which quickly switches to the "real" `Destination` once `NavHostController` catches up with itself and returns the true `non-null` value, was causing these UI elements to flash on the screen before going away, when they should have instead just not been there at all.
- Rename `AlarmApp` -> `TopLevelNavHost`, `NavComponent` -> `CoreScreenNavComponent`, and `CoreNavHost` -> `CoreScreenNavHost`

# Viewable Changes
* Menu tabs (food, drink, brunch, etc) are now rendered based on whatever is in the sheet
* Any data fetching page (menus and faq) now have a loading skeleton state. This removes the price flickering from setting initial state to the fallback
* FAQ is now added to nav bar. If no questions are added, which currently there are none. It will show a default message

# "Backend" changes
* moved to papa parse for generic data fetcher
* changed menu interface to just a Record instead of explicit fields for food and drink
* To prevent error from trying to render old schema cached data, if cached data is of old schema, fresh pull will be forced
* Added cache busting to FAQ page
* Updated fallback menus to new schema

author: hj-core
body:
In #11, we supplemented tests to Cache::allocate_object, and this PR improves those tests in the following aspects:
- Verify the cache remains unmodified if an error is returned.
- Verify the cache contains the expected slabs after the allocation.
- Verify the cache has the expected objects allocated after the allocation.
- Verify the name of the cache remains unmodified after the allocation.
- Verify the slab_layout of the cache remains unmodified after the allocation.

In order to limit the scope of change, we introduce a new test utility verify_cache_invariants_v2 instead of refactoring the existing one. The verify_cache_invariants_v2 will gradually replace the verify_cache_invariants as the review goes on, and eventually be renamed to get rid of the v2.

## Why I'm doing:
some load profile counters are not accumulated, such as the current pending or running tasks, the flushing memtables, etc. It also may lead to the test failure if accumulate them. For example, if `LoadChannelTestForLakeTablet.test_final_profile` gets 2 times of the profile, the `TabletsNum` will double
```
 Expected equality of these values:
   4
   replicas_profile->get_counter("TabletsNum")->value()
     Which is: 8
```

## What I'm doing:
use counter->set instead of counter->update for those counters

author: piki
body:
This adds two new tools to `pscale mcp server`:
 - `list_docs` lists [all available docs on planetscale.com/docs](https://planetscale.com/docs)
 - `get_doc` retrieves one doc from the output of `list_docs`, in Markdown format

The funny thing is, I can't get Claude to bother with this tool at all.  Here's a sample conversation:

> Give me an example of how to add a vector index with cosine distance to a PlanetScale database

It hallucinates something based on vector syntax from several other MySQL-style databases.

> That's wrong.  Check the docs.

It searches the web and provides a correct answer.

> How much memory does my instance need to build a vector index with a million rows?  Check the planetscale docs.

It searches the web and provides a correct answer.

> In the PlanetScale docs, how do I create a Metal database?

It searches the web and provides a correct answer.

---

So, I'm not convinced `list_docs` and `get_docs` are necessary -- an LLM that knows how to use those probably knows how to search the web, which accomplishes the same purpose without the ongoing costs of maintaining docs-related MCP tools and endpoints.

I really just opened this for discussion.  cc @ayrton

Name: Ankit Pasi

Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01115

Team: pasi2, sp108

High Level Description: EGMDataset class for loading and processing the
PhysioNet Intracardiac Atrial Fibrillation Database within the PyHealth framework.

File Contributed: egm_intra.py + update to requirements.py (only 1 addition of 'wfdb')

Detailed Description:
This script defines the EGMDataset class for loading and processing the
PhysioNet Intracardiac Atrial Fibrillation Database within the PyHealth framework.
It reads WFDB EGM signals, performs Z-score normalization, segments the signals
into fixed-length (potentially overlapping) windows, and assigns an AFib label
based on record comments (defaulting to 1 if indeterminate). Each signal segment
is treated as an event and organized into a Polars DataFrame following the
pyhealth.datasets.BaseDataset structure, storing the raw signal segment as an
object within the DataFrame. The script includes an example usage block/test case (`if __name__ == "__main__":`)
that can run with either user-provided data (via --data-root) or auto-generated
dummy data.

author: pockers21
body:
When the model processes multiple data batches during inference, if the first data entry has a length of 1000, the output buffer length will be calculated as (1000 × vocab_size / embd_size). After allocating the output buffer space, the system performs a full-range memset operation. However, when subsequent inference data (e.g., the second batch) has a shorter length than 1000, the memset operation still clears the entire 1000-length space, resulting in significant performance overhead.
This PR introduces dynamic length adjustment to update memset parameters based on actual data length, thereby minimizing unnecessary performance waste.

author: renato
body:
Adds support to creating an "autolink" by explicitly typing the `<https://link>`.

Changes linkification while typing to only act when `markup` is `linkify` (so, not a `[normal](link)` nor an `<autolink>`), and adds a test to make sure `<http://auto.links>` won't convert to a `linkify` while typing.

Avoids linkifying within code when pasting `text/html`.

Removes the `markup: "linkify"` when pasting a URL over a selection, as that will create a `[normal](link)` instead.

Fixes the case on Firefox when you're typing an `example.com` URL mid-paragraph and it stopped the link mark before the last letter, leaving an un-linked dangling `m`.

Also uses a `linkify.test()` call before `linkify.match()` for "best speed" as per https://markdown-it.github.io/linkify-it/doc/#LinkifyIt.prototype.match.

## ✅ 작업 분류 - [ ] 버그 수정 - [x] 신규 기능 - [ ] 프로젝트 구조 변경 - [ ] 코드 리팩토링 - [ ] 기능 수정
## ✨ 작업 내용 1. 마이페이지 수정 서비스 로직 작성 2. 토큰 생성 시, kakaoId가 아니라 사용자의 기본키를 바탕으로 생성하도록 변경
## 👥 전달사항 1. 현재는 주소와 서비스만 수정할 수 있도록 작성되었습니다. 다른 필드들에 대하여 수정이 필요하다면, 추가적으로 개발하도록 하겠습니다.
## ✅ 체크리스트 - [x] 코드가 컴파일 및 빌드됨 - [x] 모든 테스트가 통과함 - [x] 관련 문서가 업데이트됨 - [x] 코드 리뷰가 수행됨 - [x] 커밋 메시지를 확인함

author: jasperf
body:
This pull request introduces significant improvements to the `Sage Native Block Package`, including enhanced documentation, new scaffolding features for Gutenberg blocks, and codebase cleanup. The changes streamline block creation, improve usability, and remove unused code for better maintainability.

### Enhancements to Documentation and Features
* Updated `README.md` to provide detailed instructions on creating and managing Gutenberg blocks, including new commands for scaffolding blocks with custom names, vendor prefixes, and skipping confirmation prompts. Added explanations of block structure and file organization. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L3-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L21-R105)

### New Block Scaffolding Features
* Added stubs for block files (`block.json`, `editor.css`, `editor.jsx`, `index.js`, `save.jsx`, `style.css`, `view.js`) to streamline block creation. These include default metadata, editor and frontend styles, React components, and client-side scripts. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-74735791078cb87bf36e4af5ba9cd5cf9ce81a1e2ce11a0757fb1e31bf0d6489R1-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7fe48c7b547ee3f6bc005f4a1121fd8d25a7f4f40740b1cbb215e8f26d93fabfR1-R13) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0247b1de7e3491e843a999348c9a7aa860a218f125ffb87e9d94429945daa4adR1-R19) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-790699a069f821fe7d9547718b5631b4420422c09bd7f3ab0261df271a6bb1bfR1-R20) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-9aaa621cad18254dd746f07a5e964317c1e30c2a389cd8f74ed3e0533466f0d6R1-R17) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-af07dfe594db4372a7005e6386461cc4c4c47be316515196c18930002f09e03eR1-R24) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-2009271f9cfe07790c58552aa0d1d9af2af41b708421b1fe8411077781669fcfR1-R27)

### Codebase Cleanup and Simplification
* Removed the `SageNativeBlock` class and its dependencies, along with unused methods in `SageNativeBlockServiceProvider`, such as singleton registration and view loading. This simplifies the codebase by eliminating unnecessary components. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-83c8dda35f3dd9e127400d2f2399d4a06397337996d861e22f8644c9587c0561L1-L39) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-30729da4290aa7d33604c1219ccd267b40ed9a6b0791a33ac51b1810d59f17fbL7) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-30729da4290aa7d33604c1219ccd267b40ed9a6b0791a33ac51b1810d59f17fbL18-L21) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-30729da4290aa7d33604c1219ccd267b40ed9a6b0791a33ac51b1810d59f17fbL39-L48)
* Updated the configuration file `config/sage-native-block.php` to remove example content and prepare for future configuration options.

### Development Tooling
* Added `laravel/pint` as a development dependency in `composer.json` for code formatting.

These changes improve the usability, maintainability, and developer experience of the package.

author: derklaro
body:
The old event system was quite outdated on the way how event updates to receive were selected. The events could only be filtered by server and had to be provided during the initial connection in the query string. The new event system addresses this problem in the following ways:
1. For subscriptions a text message must now be sent to the client, allowing to change subscriptions without reconnecting.
2. Data can now be filtered by their respective journey/dispatch post id as well, allowing to only subscribe to updates of a single journey rather than all journeys on a server
3. Subscriptions can now be removed again without needing to reconnect by sending a text message
4. The whole event system is now documented for other developers to easily understand how to access data

author: galaio
body:
This PR will add new blcok fetching mechanism, it will reduce the block fetching time cost a lot.

## Motivation

With the future activation of BEP-520 and BEP-524, BSC will achieve a subsecond block interval, which has higher requirements for faster block fetching.

However, the eth/68 protocol is very inefficient when processing NewBlockHash messages, and it requires multiple queries before a new block can be imported.

## Summary

This BEP introduces a New Block Fetching Message, which greatly reduces the number of queries, supports fast fetching of newly generated blocks, avoids validators and full nodes from lagging behind in the subsecond block interval, and especially improves the validator consensus efficiency, which can produce the next block or send vote faster.

This PR refactors the `state_transition` file. This was to make it easier to maintain this code and bring future changes and updates. I'm deriving this from my experience working on [rollup-geth](https://github.com/NethermindEth/rollup-geth) and implementing various EIPs/RIPs such as [EIP-7706](https://github.com/NethermindEth/rollup-geth/pull/22)

I tried to make this PR small so that it's easy to review and give feedback on whether you like these changes. 
The general overview of the PR:
1. There is a lot of gas handling logic, all of which has been moved to `state_transition_gas.go`
2. I have extracted hardfork-specific _stuff_ to separate functions, e.g., `preCheckGasLondon`. The benefit of this is that the logic is well contained, the caller functions are smaller, and it'll be easier to add new hardfork logic in the future
3. Some functions could've been split even further, but I didn't want to overkill it 😅 
4. I haven't changed the _flow_ of the logic, nor added any new _features_
5. All tests pass

P.S.
I've opened the PR from personal fork instead from [rollup-geth fork](https://github.com/NethermindEth/rollup-geth), as it was easier for me to do so.

body:
# PR: Add `course_scores` Table + Minor Schema Improvements

### IMPORTANT NOTE: Please delete your data.db file before running setup.py again

## Overview

This PR updates the backend schema and data-pulling logic to support eventual display of per-course scores on the frontend (as seen in Forum). These updates are backend-only and don’t touch any frontend components (yet).

I wanted to push these backend changes early so we all have time to rerun `setup.py`, and so we’re all aligned before integrating this with frontend changes (especially with ongoing work Lina is doing there).

---

## Summary of Changes

### Schema + Data Changes

- Added `user_id` to the `outcome_assessments` table to store our own internal student IDs. This might be useful when adding links to assignments
- Renamed `target_assignment_group_id` → `assignment_group_id` for clarity and concision
- Created a new `course_scores` table, populated using the same final score logic that appears in Forum (pre-bonus/penalty)

  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS course_scores (
      course_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
      term_id INTEGER,
      score REAL,
      updated_on TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  );

### Future Frontend Addition
- On the "By Course" frontend tab, this could be added as a third column (maybe called something like `Course Score`)

### Notes on Course Scores

- The new `score` field reflects the overall course average as displayed on Forum
- This is before any late/absence penalties or extension bonuses are applied

### More console logging
- Added a few more console logs (after terms are inserted) so the user feels like something is actually happening during longer backend setup steps lol

---

### Abandoned Attempt: Absences & Extensions

- I explored pulling attendance/extension data from Forum, but found it’s only available for the current term
- Since there’s no historical data exposed through the API or UI (that I could find), I decided not to store it
- We can revisit this if we ever find a more complete data source or want to show only current-term data

body:
### Packages impacted by this PR
@azure/cosmos

### Issues associated with this PR


### Describe the problem that is addressed by this PR

This PR introduces support for Per Partition Automatic Failover (PPAF) and Per Partition Circuit Breaker (PPCB) into the JavaScript SDK for Azure Cosmos DB.

Overview: PPAF enhances the resiliency of Cosmos DB accounts by enabling automatic failover at the partition level. When a partition loses quorum or becomes unavailable in one region, PPAF allows the system to automatically promote a healthy replica in another region to take over operations without any required application changes. This ensures that if a server or region goes offline, data remains accessible, and the application continues to function without disruption. Reads and writes can automatically be routed to a healthy region. Per Partition Circuit Breaker (PPCB) is a feature aimed at optimizing read availability in single master accounts and read + write availability in multi master accounts during partition outages or quorum loss.

This PR gives the SDK ability to :

1. Detect partition-level failures and discover the new region for failed over partition. Once failover conditions are met, the SDK triggers a partition level override to the next preferred region.
2. Route subsequent document requests to the new region for the failed over partition.
3. Failback to the original region for that partition.
4. Run a background task that periodically checks connection status to initiate failback for single master read requests and multi master read and write requests. 

This PR includes the following changes to implement PPAF and PPCB in the JavaScript SDK:

Failover Detection Logic: Added logic to detect partition-level failures and redirect traffic to healthy replicas.
Retry Logic: Extended SDK's retry logic to handle service unavailable errors and ensure write availability.
Background Task: Implemented background task to periodically check connection status and initiate failback.
These changes ensure that the JavaScript SDK can leverage PPAF and PPCB to enhance the availability and reliability of Azure Cosmos DB,

# Issue
On Large sites, AR / AP consumes quite a lot of memory. It sometimes lead to connection being closed as the process is killed by kernel OOM. This is due to the report design, which fetches the whole Payment Ledger table for processing.

# Interim Fix
Framework has a feature called Unbuffered cursor, which returns results as an iterator. But internally, this fetches records in batched manner (1000).

Report has been refactored to make use of this option.  `Account Settings` will allow users to select fetching method.

author: mitschabaude
body:
This PR finishes a project that has been core to our library from the beginning: **"Intransparency" of subcircuits**.

In other words, when doing a proof about circuit A, we should not have to reason about what exactly is going on in A's subcircuits.

The final missing piece in this project was the `Environment.uses_local_witnesses` statement. So far, this statement was directly referencing the _entire_ vector of witnesses created inside a circuit.

This PR instead defines `uses_local_witnesses` inductively, and for subcircuits replaces it with a custom statement, in the same way we already do for `constraints_hold`.

* for **FormalCircuit**, we use the statement `assumptions -> spec`.
  * Note that this complements the `constraint_holds.completeness` statement, which is just `assumptions`. In the proof of a parent circuit, after you have proven a subcircuit's `assumptions`, you can use the `assumptions -> spec` implication to also use the `spec` in the rest of your proof.
* for **FormalAssertion**, we just ignore the statement and replace it with `True`
  * In the completeness proof for assertions, you already have to prove `assumptions AND spec`, and there is no way to strengthen that even further.

With that change, completeness proofs become much easier. To demonstrate this, we add a completeness proof for the Keccak `theta` gadget which is just a single `simp_all` call.

# Add Fields for Trading Volume Data to Subgraph [SF-1341]

This PR implements the requirements described in SF-1341 to track trading volumes:

1. **Cumulative Trading Volume by User and Currency**
   - Added `TakerVolumeByCurrency` entity to track each user's taker-side trading volume by currency
   - Note: Due to the lazy evaluation methodology in the orderbook system, only taker information is available when orders are executed, not maker information

2. **Total Trading Volume by Currency across the Protocol**
   - Added `ProtocolVolumeByCurrency` entity that relates to the Protocol entity
   - Tracks total volume traded for each currency across the entire platform

3. **24-Hour Trading Volume for Each Orderbook**
   - Leverages the existing `DailyVolume` entity which already tracks daily volumes per lending market

## Implementation Notes

- Named the user volume entity `TakerVolumeByCurrency` to be explicit about the limitation of only tracking taker volumes
- Extended the existing `Protocol` entity rather than creating a standalone entity for total volumes
- Updated all relevant event handlers to track volumes: `handleOrderExecuted`, `handlePositionUnwound`, and `handleItayoseExecuted`
- Fixed type issues in the initializer.ts file to ensure compatibility with TypeScript

## Example GraphQL Queries

To query total trading volume by currency:
```graphql
{
  protocolVolumesByCurrencies {
    currency
    totalVolume
  }
}
```

To query a user's taker trading volumes:
```graphql
{
  takerVolumesByCurrencies(where: { user: "0x..." }) {
    currency
    totalVolume
  }
}
```

To query 24-hour volume for a specific lending market:
```graphql
{
  dailyVolumes(where: { currency: "0x...", day: "2025-04-17" }) {
    volume
  }
}
```

상품이 생성될 때 최저가에 해당 상품을 반영하기 위한 이벤트 처리가 필요했습니다. 그래서 상품 도메인에서 발생하는 생성 이벤트를 프로모션 도메인에서 받아 판매 상품에 저장하고, 최저가 Redis 검증에 반영하는 로직을 작성했습니다.

## 📝 작업 내용
### 변경 사항
- 카프카 컨슈머 설정 추가
- 상품 이벤트 컨슘 로직 추가
- 상시 판매에 추가된 상품 등록 로직 추가
- Redis 최저가 업데이트 이벤트 발행
- Redis 최저가 업데이트 로직 추가

### 변경 이유

### 추가 설명

## 💬리뷰 요구사항

#### #️⃣ 연관된 이슈
closed #59 

## PR 유형

이 PR은 어떤 변경 사항을 포함하고 있나요?

- [x] 새로운 기능 추가
- [ ] 버그 수정

- [ ] 코드에 영향을 주지 않는 변경사항 (오타 수정, 탭 사이즈 변경, 변수명 변경 등)

- [ ] 주석 추가 및 수정

- [ ] 빌드 부분 혹은 패키지 매니저 수정

## ✅ Check List

PR이 다음 요구 사항을 충족하는지 확인하세요.

- [x] 커밋 메시지 컨벤션에 맞게 작성했습니다.
- [ ] 변경 사항에 대한 테스트를 했습니다. (버그 수정/기능에 대한 테스트)

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **신규 기능**
  - Kafka 연동 및 소비자/이벤트 핸들러 도입으로 외부 상품 생성 이벤트를 수신하고 자동으로 프로모션에 상품을 추가할 수 있습니다.
  - 프로모션 관리용 REST API(최저가 갱신 트리거) 및 Kafka 관련 설정/환경설정 추가.
  - 프로모션 상품 추가, 할인율 갱신 등 이벤트 기반 비동기 처리 지원.

  - 할인율 입력값의 유효성 범위가 0~99로 변경되어 0 할인율 허용.

  - 프로모션 상품(productId) 컬럼에 유니크 제약조건 추가.

- **기타**
  - SQL 시드 데이터 최신화(프로모션 기간 연장 및 신규 프로모션/상품 추가).
  - Kafka, Redis 등 외부 시스템 연동을 위한 설정 및 의존성 추가.

author: amanmahe
body:
This PR includes the following updates and improvements:

NPG-Lite Connectivity:

   - Implemented connection logic for NPG-Lite over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
   - Abstracted connection logic using a shared interface for all transport types.
 
Live Streaming Layer (LSL) Integration:

   - Automatically starts LSL stream upon successful connection.
   - Streams real-time data from NPG-Lite over LSL.


UI Enhancements:

1. Added real-time display for:

   - Connection Status
   - Sampling Rate
   - Samples Lost
   - LSL Status

2. Improved UX to reflect data flow and streaming activity clearly after connection.

@lorforlinux, please review and merge it.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added support for WiFi and Bluetooth device connections alongside serial.
  - Introduced BLE device scanning, connection, and streaming capabilities.
  - Enhanced UI with connection type selection, real-time status, sampling rate, sample loss, and LSL stream info.
  - Added window controls: always-on-top toggle, minimize, and close.

- **Improvements**
  - Refined device detection and streaming logic for asynchronous operation and robust error handling.
  - Updated global styles for improved layout and transparency.
  - Updated application window configuration for transparency, fixed size, and non-resizability.
  - Expanded capability and permission settings for window and event management.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Unified build artifact paths and simplified build step conditions in the build workflow.

- **Chores**
  - Updated dependencies and package versions.
  - Cleaned up formatting, whitespace, and resource references in build and output files.

- **Documentation**
  - Removed macOS-specific installation instructions from the README.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

This fixes the bug reported by Loredana with the new navigator plugin:

If the label data is loaded as 2D images, but the image data is loaded as 3D data with singleton Z dimension, the position event returns 3D positions, while the label scale was a 2D array. This is now handled explicilty

## 📋 Description

Github Issue Fixes: [PSMRI/AMRIT/87](https://github.com/PSMRI/AMRIT/issues/87)
JIRA ID:

This PR introduces commit message standardization for the ⁠Helpline104-API project by setting up Commitlint, Husky, and Commitizen. The goal is to enforce a consistent commit message format across the repository to improve collaboration, readability, and enable automation (like changelogs and versioning) in the future.

These tools are now fully integrated:

- Commitlint enforces conventional commit message structure
- Husky prevents non-compliant commits by using Git hooks
- Commitizen provides an easy, interactive CLI for making properly formatted commits
- GitHub Actions validate commit messages for all pull requests

---

- [x] 🐞 **Bug fix** (non-breaking change which resolves an issue)
- [x] ✨ **New feature** (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

- [ ] 🛠 **Refactor** (change that is neither a fix nor a new feature)
- [x] ⚙️ **Config change** (configuration file or build script updates)
- [ ] 📚 **Documentation** (updates to docs or readme)
- [ ] 🧪 **Tests** (adding new or updating existing tests)
- [ ] 🎨 **UI/UX** (changes that affect the user interface)
- [ ] 🚀 **Performance** (improves performance)
- [x] 🧹 **Chore** (miscellaneous changes that don't modify src or test files)

---

## ℹ️ Additional Information

Added Configuration Files

- commitlint.config.js - Defines commit message validation rules
- .husky/commit-msg - Hook that runs validation on commit messages
- .github/workflows/commitlint.yml - GitHub Actions workflow for PR validation

Dependencies Added

- @commitlint/cli and @commitlint/config-conventional - For commit message linting
- commitizen and cz-conventional-changelog - For guided commit creation

Package.json Updates

- Added commit script for easy Commitizen access
- Configured Commitizen adapter settings
- Ensured compatibility with existing scripts

Testing Completed

- Successfully blocked malformed commit messages locally
- Generated proper commits using the new tooling
- Verified GitHub Actions correctly validate PR commits
- Ensured compatibility with existing development workflows

<!-- 感谢你的贡献 -->

## 动机

<!-- 请在这里描述你的修改 -->
<!-- 如果有相关讨论 issue 请链接到该处 -->
<!-- 如 fixes #59，这将会在本 PR 合并后自动 close 该 issue -->
<!-- 当然，如果这不是一个 bug fix 的 PR，请使用 closes #59 -->
<!-- 或者如果本 PR 只是与该 issue 相关，并没有完全解决该 issue 的话，请使用其他符号 -->
<!-- 如 related to #59 -->


- [x] feat: 添加 `--parse-resources` 参数. 解析包含的资源项目但不下载。parse 时 show play url, video_quality, audio_quality, metadata, cover_link)
- [x] refact:  将 `cover_data` 的下载移动至 `start_downloader` 中.


在 parse 时解析出来的 `play url` (可以二次解析进而单独下载), 可以把 `batch` 性质的任务转化为 `single` ,比如如果在 WebUI 中，可以进行手动选集(原本收藏夹和合集和 space 是不能选集的)。或者如果要支持 toml 任务列表，也可以先把所有任务解析为 `play url` 然后一个一个下载。而不用考虑 batch single 混合时问题。
提前显示 metadata , cover_link 这些则是我在 WebUI 中可以描述一下解析出来的 url 对应的是啥。

cover 本身并不小， 如果在解析的时候下载，会严重拖慢解析速度， 并且似乎还会引起风控，过高的请求频率。所以把 cover_link 单独传递到 start_downloader 进行下载。



## 解决方案

<!-- 如果你的 PR 改动内容较多，请在这里详述你的解决方案 -->

### 1. --parse-reousrces

本质是 `return DownloadState.SKIP` 来跳过音视频下载。并且通过 `parse_resources:bool` 来控制 `show metadata ,  cover_link , url` 等信息。

提取出来 url 都对应的是 playing_url :

- ugc_video :  https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1vZ4y1M7mQ?p=1
- bangumi : https://www.bilibili.com/bangumi/play/ep1448960
- cheese: https://www.bilibili.com/cheese/play/ep487830

它们有个特点就是都可以 `yutto url` 进行单独下载。那么就可以通过二次解析来手动选集。

使用方式:

yutto.toml(因为基本都不用额外下载，所以我把所有资源选项都设置为 true , 设置一些 false 则不会解析那些。):

```toml
[basic]
num_workers = 8
video_quality = 80
audio_quality = 30280
sessdata = "=-="
vip_strict = false
login_strict = false
dir = "./downloads"

[resource]
require_video = true # video_quality
require_audio = true # audio_quality
require_danmaku = true 
require_subtitle = true
require_metadata = true # show metadata
require_cover = true # show cover_link
save_cover = false
```

command:

```shell
uv run yutto -b --parse-resources https://www.bilibili.com/bangumi/play/ss81007/
```
```shell
uv run yutto  --parse-resources https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1hzADeFEvA/
```


### 2. cover_data -> cover_link

延迟 cover_data 的下载。

A small `PR` to introduce a `property` to drive `jte` stack dependencies version.
As the `maven` plugin and the `starter` must have the same version, we now are sure to always use correlated dependencies.

The explicit dependency declaration of `gg.jte:jte` has been removed as it is a transitive dependency of `gg.jte:jte-spring-boot-starter-3`.

Using `properties` to drive third-party dependencies version not managed in `springboot-bom` is helpful:
- open the possibility to check for new version locally via `mvn versions:display-property-updates`
- simplify reviews of `Dependabot` (or any other tool we would like to use) `PRs`

### User Service Enhancements:

### Configuration and Setup:

### Testing and Workflow Updates:

author: ematipico
body:
<!--
	Thanks for submitting a Pull Request! We appreciate you spending the time to work on these changes.
	Please provide enough information so that others can review your PR.
	Once created, your PR will be automatically labeled according to changed files.
	Learn more about contributing: https://github.com/biomejs/biome/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Summary

Part of #5636 

This PR introduces a new domain called `RuleDomain::Project` (we can bikeshed the name). This domain is used to mark rules that require type information or module graph information. Essentially, those slow rules where Biome needs to scan the whole project, collect info, and run them.

- For users: we can now document those rules on our website and thoroughly explain the implications of enabling the rules that belong to this new domain.
- For us maintainers: to panic in case we add a rule requiring type/graph information and forget to add it to the correct domain. I chose the runtime + panic route because we need to catch these cases early. Just forgetting one can have serious repercussions on our end users. 


This PR also creates a new function called `compute_scan_kind` that tells Biome what scanning needs to be triggered. Other than checking the CLI commands, it now checks the configuration, and if there's at least one rule that uses `RuleDomain::Project`, it returns `ScanKind::Project`.

<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve?-->

<!-- Link any relevant issues if necessary or include a transcript of any Discord discussion. -->

## Test Plan

In this repository, we use the rule `noImportCycles`. When disabled, I could see that the CLI takes way less time. When enabled, it takes more time.

I added new tests for `compute_scan_kind`

author: xabg2
body:
This RP gets the correct customer when trying to get the customer ID to make a payment. For this case, what we do is the following:
- We check that it exists in the local database using the uuid. If it exists, we return the existing one.
- If it does not exist by uuid, we obtain the customerIds associated to the user's email in Stripe.
- If it has any customerId, we check if any of them match with the one we have in the local database. If it is the case, we check if the uuid matches. If they do not match, then we update the uuid of that item in the collection and return the existing customer Id. 

If none of the above steps is successful, then we create a customer id.

body:
This pull request introduces a new "Releases" section to the Astreos website, updates the navigation structure, and improves the overall user experience with various enhancements. The most significant changes include adding a breadcrumb navigation system, creating a dedicated layout for release notes, and updating asset paths for consistency.

### New Features and Enhancements:

* **Releases Section and Layouts:**
  - Added a new `releases.json` file to include release metadata.
  - Created a `release-notes.md` file and a `post.html` layout to display release notes with download links for Windows, macOS, and Linux. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-82200ce47fa528129da57d8979b63119ebdc262e3d07cb7882fdb8d1ecdf4a00R1-R49) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-88e83e5d0edb4286d0e35534fa9f49405a4ef6724137b468772a31183cb43a3fR1-R52)
  - Introduced a new `releases/index.html` page to showcase release notes in a structured format.

* **Breadcrumb Navigation:**
  - Implemented breadcrumb navigation for better usability in the `post.html` layout.

### Navigation and Asset Path Updates:

* **Navbar Updates:**
  - Updated the navbar to include a "Releases" link, conditionally displayed if posts exist.
  - Adjusted the navbar brand link to use `relative_url` for better compatibility.

* **Asset Path Standardization:**
  - Standardized asset paths across the site to remove the `/astreos-dev` prefix, ensuring consistency. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-59d7533953135e1ecd90fda6cbbe9f578fb34255fb782d4f072d896ab8465a7eL7-R34) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-59d7533953135e1ecd90fda6cbbe9f578fb34255fb782d4f072d896ab8465a7eL98-R111) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-59d7533953135e1ecd90fda6cbbe9f578fb34255fb782d4f072d896ab8465a7eL116-R121) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-59d7533953135e1ecd90fda6cbbe9f578fb34255fb782d4f072d896ab8465a7eL126-R131) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-59d7533953135e1ecd90fda6cbbe9f578fb34255fb782d4f072d896ab8465a7eL136-R141) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-59d7533953135e1ecd90fda6cbbe9f578fb34255fb782d4f072d896ab8465a7eL148-R153) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-59d7533953135e1ecd90fda6cbbe9f578fb34255fb782d4f072d896ab8465a7eL157-R162)

### Third-Party Integration:

* **Font Awesome:**
  - Integrated Font Awesome for icons used in download buttons and other UI elements. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-907a69846a1f6b238f1c43199984197d12c7eab26f3c3adcd45d628b26644950R31-R34) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-59d7533953135e1ecd90fda6cbbe9f578fb34255fb782d4f072d896ab8465a7eL7-R34)

These changes collectively enhance the website's functionality, navigation, and user experience while preparing it for future updates and release management.

author: nrheckman-afero
body:
The GlobalConfigurationBuilder read(GlobalConfiguration template) method requires that classes registered as modules be annotated with @BuiltBy at runtime.
Without the required annotation, a NullPointerException is observed.

Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "org.infinispan.commons.configuration.BuiltBy.value()" because "builtBy" is null

The simple fix here is to add the missing annotation. I tested this locally and observed that the configured metrics registry is used.

author: manoguar
body:
This PR replaces the original implementation of the `PrivateKey` class with a secure, immutable version that eliminates unsafe public exposure of sensitive cryptographic material.

### Summary of changes:
- Removed `DebuggerDisplay` and `ToString()` that previously exposed the Base58-encoded private key.
- Replaced mutable public properties (`Key`, `KeyBytes`) with a single immutable backing field and safe readonly access.
- Enforced strict immutability after construction.
- Lazy Base58 encoding with internal caching (`GetBase58()`), no longer exposed via `ToString()`.
- Updated `Equals()` to perform byte-level comparison rather than string-based.
- Replaced `GetHashCode()` with a fast, consistent implementation derived from internal key bytes.
- Signature logic remains intact (`Sign()` using `Ed25519.Sign`).

### Notes:
- **This breaks tests/examples** that relied on the insecure `.ToString()` or public access to `Key`. This is intentional.
- Key exposure through debugger/logging is now fully eliminated.
- No functional change to wallet creation, signing, or keypair loading.

This refactor lays groundwork for improving keystore handling, memory hygiene, and test coverage without leaking sensitive material.

Let me know if you'd like this split further or integrated into an upcoming security milestone.

body:
This pull request introduces significant enhancements to the `agentic_radar` project, focusing on improving the analysis and visualization of n8n workflows. Key changes include support for analyzing multiple workflows, incorporating node positions for better visualization, and adding filtering options for specific workflows. Additionally, a new visualization module has been introduced to generate graphical representations of workflows.

### Enhancements to n8n workflow analysis:

* [`agentic_radar/analysis/analyze.py`](diffhunk://#diff-225493b21c4945329d27a9b2d9f2127279644660a8a454c598ff5ade12d8ffd5R2-R8): Updated the `Analyzer` interface to support returning a list of `GraphDefinition` objects, enabling analysis of multiple workflows.
* [`agentic_radar/analysis/n8n/analyze.py`](diffhunk://#diff-78317a4d941fd906e077a601fa873ecd5b89bcc9a5b042f0ee428e6daed55282L3-R185): Refactored the `N8nAnalyzer` class to include filtering options (`connected_only`, `langchain_only`) and added support for handling workflows with position data. Enhanced logging for better debugging and added a mechanism to ensure all nodes referenced in edges are included in the graph.

### Support for node positions:

* [`agentic_radar/analysis/n8n/models.py`](diffhunk://#diff-1479653894735388f70a9fa50d3331ba397a7fc3dca704519e60d066d3b32565R10): Added a `position` attribute to the `N8nNode` model to store node coordinates.
* [`agentic_radar/analysis/n8n/converter.py`](diffhunk://#diff-74fcc89984b70f704eb258e733bf371468f674e31f50dcea25ba732dc260172aR16): Modified the `convert_nodes` function to process and scale position data for nodes, ensuring layout consistency in visualizations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-74fcc89984b70f704eb258e733bf371468f674e31f50dcea25ba732dc260172aR16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-74fcc89984b70f704eb258e733bf371468f674e31f50dcea25ba732dc260172aR31-R42) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-74fcc89984b70f704eb258e733bf371468f674e31f50dcea25ba732dc260172aR51-R52) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-74fcc89984b70f704eb258e733bf371468f674e31f50dcea25ba732dc260172aR62-R63) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-74fcc89984b70f704eb258e733bf371468f674e31f50dcea25ba732dc260172aR72-R84)

### Visualization improvements:

* [`agentic_radar/analysis/n8n/visualization.py`](diffhunk://#diff-e4844efdeb4e243745fbad39dcaef2c1c385f2c6ad2610f4a86db75381601e84R1-R158): Introduced a new module for generating visual representations of workflows using `networkx` and `matplotlib`. Supports both position-based layouts and fallback spring layouts.

### CLI updates:

* [`agentic_radar/cli.py`](diffhunk://#diff-0d0fc9a10f46b8d0d8951348a68b2e9eded007e0fa99d8cc226c8632725a0065L83-R101): Enhanced the CLI to handle multiple workflows, generate unique report filenames, and support new options (`--connected-only`, `--langchain-only`, `--use-n8n-positions`) for filtering and layout customization. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0d0fc9a10f46b8d0d8951348a68b2e9eded007e0fa99d8cc226c8632725a0065L83-R101) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0d0fc9a10f46b8d0d8951348a68b2e9eded007e0fa99d8cc226c8632725a0065L108-R129) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0d0fc9a10f46b8d0d8951348a68b2e9eded007e0fa99d8cc226c8632725a0065L124-R169)

### Parsing enhancements:

author: ashad001
body:
This PR introduces major improvements to the feedback system and login flow:

### 📝 Feedback Form Enhancements
- **Larger Form UI:**  
  - Dialog size increased to `sm:max-w-2xl`  
  - Taller textarea (6 rows)  
  - Scrollable feedback modal with `max-h-[90vh]`  
- **Image Upload Support:**  
  - Drag-and-drop zone for image attachments  
  - Direct clipboard paste support for screenshots  
  - Preview grid with remove functionality  
  - Limit: 5 images, max 5MB each  
- **Email Integration:**  
  - API now handles multipart form data with attachments  
  - Emails include image attachments and image count visual  
  - All feedback is properly formatted and sent via `SMTP_USER`

### 🧠 Session Info in Feedback Emails
- **Automatic Context Collection:**  
  - Session ID, user email (via NextAuth), dataset, model/provider info  
  - Last 2 chat queries using the existing API  
- **Enhanced Email Formatting:**  
  - "Session Information" and "Recent Chats" sections  
  - Easy-to-read formatting with timestamps and chat titles  
- **Technical Details:**  
  - Typed all structures for TS safety  
  - Fallbacks for missing data + error handling for API/JSON

### 🔄 Login Page Redirection Logic
- Integrated `useSearchParams` to parse `redirect` URL  
- Dynamically updates `redirectUrl` for Google and admin login  
- Maintains smooth flow: e.g., from pricing → login → auto-redirect to checkout

author: lfarrel6
body:
# Why

Releases being created on publish contain the entirety of a packages changes instead of the details for the release in question

# How

For a release commit, take the diff of the changelog file, strip the diff formatting, and use it as the changelog content.

author: tobz
body:
## Summary

As part of our internal metrics, we have to collect and translate metrics from their native `metrics` format into our internal metrics format. Doing so primarily requires collapsing "labels" (`metrics` parlance), which are individual key/value pairs, into our internal tags (`saluki` parlance), which are single values that are either bare keys (like `env`), or concatenated key/value pairs (like `env:prod`). As we have to do this every single time we try to resolve a context via `ContextResolver`, we lose out on a lot of the potential savings of getting a cached context as we're still allocating a bunch of strings to hold the concatenated labels/tags.

This PR wraps `ContextResolver` and combines it with a simple cache, which maps the metrics "key" (`metrics::Key`, the equivalent of `saluki_context::Context`) to the context, but uses `ContextResolver` for uncached contexts so that we still intern strings, handle origin detection, and so on.

This should hopefully both reduce on-going allocations to nearly zero after all internal metrics have been seen at least once, which in turn should help reduce the tail latency of collecting internal metrics.

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Non-functional (chore, refactoring, docs)
- [x] Performance

Ran ADP locally and ensured internal metrics still showed up as expected when scraping the telemetry endpoint.

For the auth system I chose to go with [better-auth](https://www.better-auth.com) and for the payment system, I chose to go with [polar.sh](https://polar.sh).

There is an already existing integration between the two, [maintained by the polar team](https://github.com/polarsource/polar-adapters/tree/main/packages/polar-betterauth), as a [better-auth plugin](https://www.better-auth.com/docs/concepts/plugins).
It's documented on both sides [polar's docs](https://docs.polar.sh/integrate/sdk/adapters/better-auth) and [better-auth's docs](https://www.better-auth.com/docs/concepts/plugins).

## Why Better-auth?

 - Framework agnostic
 - We control our users (can adapt to pretty much any DB)
 - Simple integration & flexible management

## Why Polar?

 - MoR simplifies the accounting side
 - 20% less than other MoRs
 - EU-based (Sweden)
 - Open Source (Apache-2.0)

This PR implements an integration for our Next.js application, it uses the [better-auth Next.js](https://www.better-auth.com/docs/integrations/next) integration, and then uses the [polar better-auth](https://docs.polar.sh/integrate/sdk/adapters/better-auth#configuration-options) integration on top of that.

## Things to sort out

 - What signin methods do we want to support? better-auth supports [a number of them (see sidebar)](https://www.better-auth.com/docs/authentication/email-password)
 - We will need to build a couple of pages
  - After payment page
  - Subscription status link (/api/auth/portal/)
  - Use the subscription status to decide when to show the code examples or not for pro stuff
 - Where to host the DB (I'm biased to self-host as this will be VERY low-traffic)

author: tobz
body:
## Summary

This PR reorganizes some of the "internal", non-data pipeline-oriented aspects of the ADP binary to better isolate their behavior from one another. This is meant to ensure that issues/degradation in the primary topology don't negatively impact the control plane, such as by preventing internal telemetry from being scraped due to topology stalls, as well as isolate the primary topology from control plane computation, such as high duration task polls which can drive up tail latency for sensitive tasks (like DogStatsD I/O handlers).

Specifically, we now isolate internal processes -- (un)privileged APIs, health registry, internal telemetry pipeline, etc -- within dedicated current-thread async runtimes. This lets us keep our existing code and utilize existing paradigms, but simply isolates the related work/tasks to their own runtime executor threads.

Notable changes:

- `bin/agent-data-plane/src/internal` now holds all internal-y things, and `bin/agent-data-plane/src/api` has been folded into it
- topologies are now named as we now run two distinct topologies (primary and internal telemetry) by default (so `topology.primary.components.sources.dsd_in` instead of `topology.components.sources.dsd_in`)
- the global event buffer pool sizing can now be configured on `TopologyBlueprint` (necessary for being able to build the internal telemetry topology while not having a firm upper bound of like 80MB)
- Tokio runtime metrics are now tagged by a `runtime_id` to allow for differentiating between the primary runtime and internal control plane runtimes
- we print the component bounds whether the bounds are satisfied or not, allowing an operator to actually understand _why_ bounds cannot be met

## Change Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Non-functional (chore, refactoring, docs)
- [x] Performance

## How did you test this PR?

Tested locally to ensure that APIs are still accessible and that internal telemetry can still be accessed/reported.

body: The numerical constant of the largest legal value in the hal type enum HAL_TYPE_MAX was, although properly placed last, not the correct value because the other enumerations were not in order while using fixed value assignments. Unassigned enums always take the "last value plus one" approach and that resulted in the wrong enum value for HAL_TYPE_MAX. The above fix exposed enum switch-cases that were not handled properly. These are fixed to use a default clause now.

If you for example create a `BoneAttachment3D` and query `"albasldasbla" in bone_attachment` it would always return true.
This is because its `_get` always reported that a property exists.

I went through all classes that override `_get` and fixed this problem everywhere I could find.
The same still has to be done for `_set` in the future (I only updated those `_set`'s on classes that had erroneous `_get`'s)!

Ideally, this could be automatically detected and reported in debug builds, by checking whether the second parameter was modified when true is returned. But that is outside of the scope of this PR.

author: timoffex
body:
DUPLICATED FROM PR #9562 which I accidentally merged into the wrong branch.

* WB-23108, WB-24208
* Docs: https://github.com/wandb/docs/pull/1145

Adds a `create_new` option to the `reinit` setting which causes `wandb.init()` to create a new run even if other runs exist. This should eventually become the default, and the other options ("return_previous" and "finish_previous") should be deprecated.

Although it's possible to pass `reinit` as a `wandb.init()` argument, the best way to use this is with `wandb.setup()`.

Here is an example that uses the `create_new` setting to (serially) run multiple sub-experiments while logging their results to another run:

```python
wandb.setup(wandb.Settings(reinit="create_new"))

with wandb.init() as experiment_results_run:
    for ...:
        with wandb.init() as run:
            # The do_experiment() function logs fine-grained metrics
            # to the given run and then returns result metrics that
            # we'd like to track separately.
            experiment_results = do_experiment(run)

            # After each experiment, we log its results to a parent
            # run. Each point in the parent run's charts corresponds
            # to one experiment's results.
            experiment_results_run.log(experiment_results)
```

---

This PR also removes `util._is_offline()` and replaces it with a heuristic that uses the newly added `most_recent_active_run`. This way, `_is_offline` continues to work as expected in most cases.

author: gatsik
body:
I encountered a very annoying issue with `isort` on Windows -- formatter always added unnecessary line after imports.

For example:
```diff
-import sys
 import os
+import sys
+
```
or
```diff
-import sys
 import os
+import sys


 def main() -> int:
+
     return 0
```
(added empty lines are redundant)

It looks like runner doesn't properly handle final `\r` on processing stdout:
```log
[TRACE] Applying text edits: { {
              newText = "os\r\nimport sys\r\n\r\n\r\ndef main() -> int:\r",
              range = {
               ...
              }
            } }
```

I came up with 2 solutions: the first one is this PR and the second one is simple:
```diff --git a/lua/conform/runner.lua b/lua/conform/runner.lua
--- a/lua/conform/runner.lua
+++ b/lua/conform/runner.lua
@@ -153,6 +153,7 @@ local function create_text_edit(
     table.insert(replacement, "")
   end
-  local new_text = table.concat(replacement, "\n")
+  local new_text = table.concat(replacement, "\n"):gsub("\r$", "")
 
   return {
     newText = new_text,
```

I don't know which one is fine (maybe neither!), but the more complex one ended up as a PR because it edits multiple files

author: jcrist
body:
Previously we would fail if the user specified `weights="distance"` to `KNeighborsClassifier`/`KNeighborsRegressor`. This fixes that and adds a test.

Part of fixing this required changing the logic in `dispatch_func` to not special-case inference methods. Previously we would always run inference on the GPU, even if `_gpuaccel` was False (meaning the hyperparameters specified weren't supported by cuml). I don't believe this to be the desired logic - if cuml doesn't support the specified hyperparameters, we cannot be sure that we do support them for `predict`. Further, the state is stored on the cpu estimator already, running inference on CPU makes more sense anyway IMO. It also makes understanding where something runs clearer:

- If the hyperparameters aren't supported by cuml, then everything runs on CPU
- If the arguments provided to a method aren't supported by cuml, then that method will dispatch to CPU
- Otherwise we run on GPU

Fixes #6545.

author: lovro-bikic
body:
This PR adds linting for whitespace after [control code](https://github.com/slim-template/slim?tab=readme-ov-file#control-code--) (`-`). With this patch, a line that doesn't have a single whitespace between `-` and the code gets registered as an offense:
```
# bad (no whitespace)
-cond

# bad (too much whitespace)
-  cond

# good (single whitespace)
- cond
```
By all accounts, this seems to be the preferred style in [slim documentation](https://github.com/slim-template/slim?tab=readme-ov-file#syntax-example).

In the implementation, I added this feature to the existing linter `ControlStatementSpacing`. I did this because linters for control code have `ControlStatement` in the name (e.g. `EmptyControlStatement`, `CommentControlStatement` or `ConsecutiveControlStatements`). Let me know if this should be moved to a new linter, although I'm not sure how I'd name it because this linter is currently used to lint [output code](https://github.com/slim-template/slim?tab=readme-ov-file#output-) instead of control code.

author: maximilianpmx
body:
This Pull Request implements basic date recognition and parsing functionality for simple date formats: 'yyyy-MM-dd' and 'MM/dd/yyyy'.

**Changes:**

*   Created a `DateParser` class with a `parseDate` method.
*   The `parseDate` method attempts to parse the input string using two predefined `DateTimeFormatter` instances for the supported formats.
*   If parsing is successful with either format, the method returns an `Optional<LocalDate>` containing the parsed date.
*   If parsing fails for both formats, the method returns an empty `Optional<LocalDate>`.
*   Added unit tests using JUnit 5 to verify the parsing logic for both supported formats, invalid formats, and empty strings.

**Testing:**

The following test cases are included in `DateParserTest.java`:

*   `parseDate_yyyy_MM_dd`: Tests parsing of dates in 'yyyy-MM-dd' format.
*   `parseDate_MM_dd_yyyy`: Tests parsing of dates in 'MM/dd/yyyy' format.
*   `parseDate_invalidFormat`: Tests parsing of dates with an unsupported format (e.g., 'yyyy/MM/dd').
*   `parseDate_emptyString`: Tests parsing of an empty string.

All tests pass, demonstrating the correct functionality of the date parsing logic.

This implementation uses `java.time.LocalDate` and `java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter` for date representation and parsing, providing a more robust and modern approach compared to older date/time APIs.

author: jlp-craigmorten
body:
## Changes

Relates to #25

- `img` element mappings now prefer `image` role over `img`, see the note in https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-img r.e. preferred synonym for WAI-ARIA 1.3
- `img` element with no `alt` attribute (i.e. missing completely) has a role of `image`, see https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-img
- `img` element with empty `alt` has a role of `none` provided the `img` does not have an accname provided by other means (e.g. `aria-label`), see https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-img-empty-alt
- `aria-label` should be trimmed of whitespace when calculating accname, see https://www.w3.org/TR/accname-1.2/#computation-steps (specifically section 2.4 of the algorithm)
- `title` should be considered when calculating accname, see https://www.w3.org/TR/accname-1.2/#computation-steps (specifically section 2.5 of the algorithm) for the core calculation and see https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-img-name for the `img` specific name calculation

## How to Review

This change was prompted by the following failing test cases taken from the [WPT roles-contextual.html suite](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html-aam/roles-contextual.html):

- el-aside-in-section-aria-label-whitespace
- el-aside-in-section-aria-labelledby-empty
- el-aside-in-section-aria-labelledby-whitespace
- el-aside-in-section-title
- el-img-empty-alt-aria-label-whitespace
- el-img-empty-alt-aria-labelledby-empty
- el-img-empty-alt-aria-labelledby-whitespace
- el-img-no-name
- el-section-aria-label-whitespace
- el-section-aria-labelledby-non-existing
- el-section-aria-labelledby-empty
- el-section-aria-labelledby-whitespace
- el-section-title

This change does not cover the following known failures:

- el-aside-in-section-aria-labelledby-non-existing
- el-img-empty-alt-aria-labelledby-non-existing
- el-th-in-row (from the [WPT table-roles.html suite](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html-aam/table-roles.html))

These would require a more accurate ACCNAME algorithm implementation for the first two, and supporting an involved algorithm to scan all rows in a table to support `rowheader` when `scope` is `auto`.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit tests updated

body:
Cette PR implémente la fonctionnalité de suppression d'un membre dans un groupe. Cette méthode vérifie plusieurs conditions avant la suppression du membre :

- La méthode vérifie si le membre existe dans le groupe. Si ce n'est pas le cas, une exception est lancée.
- Si le membre a des dettes, la suppression est bloquée, et une exception est levée.
- Si le membre existe et n'a pas de dettes, il est supprimé du groupe.

Cette PR inclus également tous les tests unitaires, d'intégration et de persistance associées.

# Description

Fixes https://github.com/mito-ds/mito/issues/1653

Before we used to scroll to the center of the cell. This would get the highlighted line in focus most of the time. 

This PR introduces a way of dynamically determine the scroll position by determining where the line is located within the cell. If the line is above the halfway mark, we scroll to the start of the cell, and if the line is below the half way mark, we scroll to the end. 

# Testing

Create a few cells with lots of content, make sure you need to scroll to see cells. Then ask a question that will return a citation. If the cell is higher up in the cell, the window should scroll so that the top of the cell is reached.

release notes 
# Backwards Incompatible Changes

There has been a type change on the `dolt_diff` system table with provides more precision and alignment with the `dolt_diff_{table}` system table. There is a remote possibility that this could impact existing applications, and client code may require updates to remain consistent.

Per [Dolt’s versioning policy](https://docs.dolthub.com/other/versioning), this is a minor version bump because these changes may impact existing applications. Please reach out to us on [GitHub](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues) or [Discord](https://discord.gg/gqr7K4VNKe) if you have questions or need help with any of these changes.

# Merged PRs

## dolt

* [9129](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/9129): More precision on the date column in the dolt_diff table
  Use higher precision date type in the `dolt_diff` table - matching `dolt_diff_{table}` now
  Fixes: https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9126

## go-mysql-server

* [2943](https://github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server/pull/2943): refactor and implement `TimestampAdd()`
  This PR implements the TimestampAdd; it is treated as basically an alias for `DateAdd()`.
  mysql docs: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/date-and-time-functions.html#function_timestampadd
  fix: https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9117
* [2940](https://github.com/dolthub/go-mysql-server/pull/2940): Bug fix: ensure `DropCheck.IfExists` gets copied over to new instances
  This change doesn't affect Dolt, but is needed by Doltgres to make sure `IF EXISTS` logic for dropping a constraint is correctly executed. 

## vitess

* [412](https://github.com/dolthub/vitess/pull/412): allow trim, cast, and position as nonkeywords
  This PR adds makes it so that `TRIM`, `CAST` and `POSITION` are usable as table and column names without backquotes.
  fixes: https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9123
* [410](https://github.com/dolthub/vitess/pull/410): fix `ntile` syntax
  This PR implements the correct syntax for `NTILE()`
  mysql docs: https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/window-function-descriptions.html#function_ntile
  syntax for: https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9087


# Closed Issues

* [9126](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9126): dolt_diff vs dolt_diff_ - commit time precision differs
* [9123](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9123): BUG: Dolt treats `position` as a reserved keyword
* [9117](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/9117): BUG: Panic in GMS when using TIMESTAMPADD()
* [6901](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/6901): sql `TIME` type is not supported in Dolt

body:
We don't need line indexing as we can fetch logs in byte blocks and trim the incomplete line.

Much better would be indexing blocks in `<plugin>.log` files that contain entry coming from specific process or even matching the specified set of methods.

This PR introduces:

- new postprocess plugin that creates an index based on Process.seqid and Method key for some plugins
- new endpoint `/logs/<task_uid>/<log_type>/process/<seqid>` that allows to fetch the filtered log. This endpoint also accepts the `filter[]=` argument that allows to filter entries with given Method names.

This includes conversion utilities to adapt Ollama's responses to the Deepseek format.

body:
## Overview
This PR introduces a new service called "Package Manager Indexer" that serves as a backend system for the Autonomys Package Registry. The indexer handles blockchain events related to tool registration and updates, stores tool data in a PostgreSQL database, and provides a RESTful API for accessing tool information.

## Key Features

### Backend Service Structure
- Set up Express.js server with proper middleware configuration
- Implemented API rate limiting (60 requests per minute per IP)
- Added stricter rate limiting (20 requests per 5 minutes) for sensitive operations
- Created robust error handling and logging system
- Configured graceful shutdown for the server

### API Endpoints
- Tool listing and search functionality
- Tool version management
- Publisher-based tool querying
- Health check and indexer status endpoints

### Blockchain Integration
- Process historical blockchain events for the AutonomysPackageRegistry contract
- Real-time monitoring of new events (ToolRegistered, ToolUpdated, OwnershipTransferred)
- Block continuity tracking and recovery mechanisms

### Database Layer
- PostgreSQL schema for tools and tool versions
- Migration system for database evolution
- Transaction handling for data integrity
- Query optimization with proper indices

### Configuration & Environment
- Added comprehensive configuration system
- Environment variable support via `.env.sample`
- Logging configuration for different environments

## Technical Details
- Transaction data parsing for blockchain events
- Semantic versioning support
- Retry mechanisms with timeout handling for blockchain operations
- Pagination support for API endpoints

## Setup Instructions
The README.md contains complete instructions for:
- Installation requirements
- Database setup
- Environment configuration
- Running the service
- API endpoint documentation

## Additional Scripts
- Database reset utility
- Indexer state reset for reprocessing blocks

## Related Changes
- Updated project tool paths
- Modified project root detection to support template projects
